task: Confirm analytics collection when the CodeMie proxy starts, with Project as the default persisted scope, a Project or Global choice during setup or reconfiguration, an Enter-to-confirm prompt, decline or cancel leaving analytics disabled for that start, silent mode skipping the prompt, and updated docs and regression coverage.

key_reasoning.reason: Setup and reconfiguration, proxy start, effective-configuration display, and the Claude Code OTLP connector must share one persisted Project/Global scope. ConfigLoader is the persistence point. The hook and daemon start paths (proxy start, connect ensure, ensureOtlpProxy) can bypass a prompt that lives on only one of them. Base L for those components plus shared config; bumped to XL because the change crosses several CLI workflows.

Seven acceptance criteria define default scope, persistence, Enter-to-confirm, decline, cancel, silent mode, docs, and regression coverage. Still open: the ticket's sample options say Enable analytics / Decline while the criteria say Confirm, and the Project sample omits the project name the criteria require. Where a decline is stored for one proxy start is unmade, because each hook is a new process and a live daemon returns before any prompt. Vocabulary already uses Global/Local for storage and user/project for the allowlist.

Closest patterns are inquirer confirm (default true, Enter confirms) and the raw-mode storage-scope chooser. Neither covers this gate: storage-scope maps ESC and Ctrl+C to Global, an empty CODEMIE_ANALYTICS_PROJECT_FILTER tracks every project (the opposite of a Project default), agent --silent is not on proxy start or the hook command, and an in-memory decline does not survive the next hook. No injection, auth, or secret-handling gap, and proxy tests already mock stdin and stdout, so those floors were not applied. Agrees with the project L anchor profile-provider-decoupling (technical risk L, total 23) and is well above the bundle M REST-endpoint example (total 15, established pattern).

About 8–10 modified files and 2 new ones across proxy commands, setup, config types, ConfigLoader, profile status, the OTLP connector, existing proxy tests, COMMANDS.md, and the project-config guide, plus a confirmation prompt module and a regression test. That is the top of L. Hook, daemon-state, and extra architecture docs stay optional until the prompt placement is decided.

CLI prompts (UI), proxy start and setup command surface (API), the daemon ensure gate (Service), and a new persisted scope on the effective configuration (persistence). Claude settings and the analytics API stay the existing integration; this does not add a new external service.

No new packages; inquirer and unused @clack/prompts are already dependencies. Scored S for a new persisted scope key. Disagrees with profile-provider-decoupling and epmcdme-10401-add-provider-with-configuration-ui, which scored dependencies XS for larger config-schema work with no new packages; the rubric's S line matches a config addition more closely than XS.

red_flags_applied: Component Scope bumped from L to XL: affects multiple workflows (setup and reconfiguration, proxy start confirmation, effective-configuration display, and the hook or daemon start path).
